name: Zephyr — options numbers layer
headline: Verification report of the options analytics landed, incl. a controlled-language copy.
about: Built the deterministic numbers layer for the options advisor — break-evens and the move to them, extrinsic, theta in $/day and the daily drift it demands, delta exposure, bounded max loss. A research pass then verified every formula against primary sources.
stopped_at: Committed docs/research/options-analytics-verification.md — 201 descriptive sentences, all style checks green.
next: Branch is clean. Decide whether it merges, or keep extending the numbers layer.

name: Mercury — seasonal menu into the POS
headline: Reconciling the spreadsheet, the till and the validated card — mid-audit.
about: Capturing the seasonal lunch and dinner menus into the item database, then pushing to the POS. Three live tabs backed up before the change and exported to the repo; nothing live overwritten.
stopped_at: First reconciliation done: the sheet holds 202 SKU / 180 active, the till 238 item cards, 48 till-only SKU in four groups. Confirmed the item CSV export silently omits deactivated items.
next: Two defects remain in the draft card. Then finish the sheet-vs-till merge.

name: KB — Mercury reporting interviews
headline: Operations wants a pre-service push, not a weekly retro — two different products.
about: Processing the reporting conversations into the knowledge base to feed what zephyr is building: the reporting call plus the voice note on table dwell time (arrival, table open, close, bill request), then the on-site session.
stopped_at: Both records written under events/. Committed to a dedicated docs/reporting branch via a throwaway worktree, so the zephyr checkout never moved.
next: Fold the finding — retrospective vs. pre-service push — into the zephyr reporting capability spec.

name: Lantern — anti-spam on the contact form
headline: Two spam levers shipped on a branch, not merged — they need your keys.
about: Started as the weekly menu sync, comparing the POS item API against the newsletter. Turned into the inbox spam question: what measures are in place, whether a captcha is needed, why the other sites are unaffected.
stopped_at: Strict origin checking rejects a POST with no real Origin header — every logged spam forges Referer and sends none, every genuine submission sent it. The captcha is wired end to end, off by default, and fails open so a provider outage can never close the form.
next: Add the captcha keys, flip strict origin on, then merge. The env example file is gitignored, so that edit is local only.

name: Beacon — mobile UI and PWA shell
headline: Deployed — safe-area insets still unverified.
about: The header ate too much of the mobile viewport. Led to a bottom nav (four slots plus a + for More), uniform icon sizing, a regenerated touch icon, and viewport-fit=cover safe-area handling.
stopped_at: Five commits deployed and verified as served. env(safe-area-inset-*) only returns real values in standalone mode, so nothing about the insets or the home-screen icon has actually been tested.
next: Delete the old home-screen entry, re-add from the browser, then check the icon, the insets and the bottom bar. The last commit is isolated and revertable on its own.
note: The ID listed first is an empty bridge stub — 7 records, no conversation. This is the real session.

name: Harbor Bot — document pipeline and auth
headline: Tasks 1-5 done and reviewed clean. 6-7 are blocked on credentials only you hold.
about: Widening the scope past the dashboard photo to the other tabs, plus the auth design: email and password, platform sign-in with private relay, invite-only for the alpha, and offline-visible persisted data with keychain storage.
stopped_at: Both branches merged into local main, 134 tests green. The Linux lane builds and tests green for the first time — identical counts to macOS. Nothing pushed.
next: Hand over the credentials for tasks 6-7, then push.

name: Toolkit — operations skill, wave 1
headline: All four wave 1 ledgers came back NOT CLEAN — and the verification is self-referential.
about: Wave 1 of the operations skill build: four jurisdiction ledgers, each verified by its own agent.
stopped_at: The harder finding is the second one: everything checked so far is ledgers against ledgers and ledgers against git history. The skill entry point has not changed since before wave 1 began. There is no ledger index and no eval set.
next: 2,570 lines across 14 planning docs and no front door. Build the eval set and a copy-pasteable resume prompt before more ledger work.

name: Chillbox — equipment rental opportunity
headline: Six-wave validation plan built. Everything hangs on turns per unit per season.
about: Assessing a rental-and-resale business for seasonal cooling equipment, off the back of a record heatwave year. Started by reviewing the evaluation prompt for blind spots.
stopped_at: The headline reference case did not survive a registry check: recently incorporated, minimal capital, zero declared headcount, no accounts filed. The revenue figures circulating are unaudited founder claims.
next: Wave 0 is free and runs this week: mystery-shop the incumbents, collect quote-only B2B prices, and send the supplier enquiries now. Below 3.5 turns per unit per season there is no business.

name: Forge — remote access after the disconnect
headline: Box reachable again via a one-word alias. Open question is the phone client.
about: Began as an investigation into why the pipe to the build box broke, ended with a working one-word reconnect in Ghostty and the whole procedure documented, plus a companion doc for phone access.
stopped_at: The previous phone client account was deleted, so that doc needs a new one. The shortlisted replacement needs no account, syncs via the platform keychain, is a one-time purchase, and mounts the box in Files.
next: Pick the client, then rewrite the phone-access doc around it.
